newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges steady, cargoes offered firmer.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges steady, cargoes offered firmer.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges closed unchanged by mid-week, but still on the upside of the past two days' trade level, while cargoes were offered firmer on the back of crude's gains and with supply said to be tight.
High sulphur fuel barges traded at $85 a tonne fob ARA for 2,000 tonnes after earlier trades at that level, which was Tuesday's close, and also $84.50 a tonne.
"The market is still balanced, about $84/$85. Demand is not too bad but is expected to improve tomorrow," a trader with a major, party to most of the higher deals recently, said.

Earlier in the day, offers were said to be in the $86 region for refining material and $85 for storage. However, a Rotterdam trader was offering high sulphur fuel directly off a ship at $84.50, traders added.
Bunker fuel prices were steady with low demand seen.
Rotterdam 380 cst bunkers were valued around $86 fob in line with prices on he ARA barge market.
Low sulphur barges were unchanged at the $95/$97 range with no deals reported in that market.
One trader said the best offer he received was at $96.50 a tonne, but no deal was done as he was not in a rush to buy.
High sulphur cargoes were firmer on the back of crude and with little material seen on offer apart from some Russian cracked fuel.
One trader was heard to be offering a cargo of M-100 at two means plus on $1. The price tag for the same cargo was a fixed $81.50 cif a day earlier.
One percent was steady to a little stronger, with some sellers seen at $95 and others at $1 over, and buyers reported to have moved up to within 50 cents of the lower price.
Some buying interest was heard to be coming in from an Italian buyer and a trader that picked up a cargo last week at $94, was also said to be active on the market seeking a second cargo.
